title: Graph Joint Representation Learning for Sound and Scalable Instantiation

problem.claim: Knowledge graph reasoning requires scalable rule instantiation while retaining interpretability and logical semantics.

gap.claim: Rule-based methods face exponential symbolic search complexity, and existing neuro-symbolic approaches struggle with complex Horn rules and rich topologies.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes Rule–Graph Joint Representation Learning, a unified neuro-symbolic framework combining rule-level reasoning with graph representation learning for scalable Horn rule instantiation.
The framework uses logically constrained rule embeddings and dominance-aware subgraph representations for embedding-guided structural pruning with exact symbolic verification.
The framework couples continuous structural abstraction with deterministic matching in a filter–verify pipeline to reduce combinatorial search while preserving logical semantics.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on large-scale knowledge graphs reportedly show consistently high accuracy and significant efficiency gains over symbolic and neuro-symbolic baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Knowledge graph reasoning is important, but symbolic methods have exponential search complexity and neuro-symbolic methods have difficulty with complex Horn rules.
The paper proposes RGRS to jointly represent rules and graphs for scalable Horn rule instantiation.
RGRS applies constrained rule embeddings and dominance-aware subgraph representations to guide structural pruning while using exact symbolic verification.
A filter–verify pipeline combines continuous structural abstraction with deterministic matching to reduce combinatorial search while preserving logical semantics.
Experiments on large-scale knowledge graphs report accuracy and efficiency advantages over symbolic and neuro-symbolic baselines.

source_observation.claim: Embedding-guided structural pruning is paired with exact symbolic verification.

interpretation.claim: A learned representation can narrow a symbolic search space while a deterministic verification stage preserves the target semantics.

application.claim: Use a filter–verify architecture when scalable approximate selection must coexist with exact rule or constraint satisfaction.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this pattern generalizes beyond Horn rule instantiation or the reported knowledge-graph settings.
